target.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's gateway validates browser `Origin` on the WebSocket path only **post-handshake** (in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts`, after the socket is already open). This leaves gaps the WebSocket upgrade phase is the only reliable place to close:

- **Header-smuggling / contradiction attacks** — a client forging `X-Forwarded-For` to disagree with `Forwarded` (or vice-versa) to confuse the resolved client IP / trust decision.
- **Cross-site WebSocket initiations (CSRF / DNS-rebinding class)** — there is no `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate anywhere in `main`.
- **Proto contradiction** — `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `Forwarded proto` disagreeing with the actual socket transport (without breaking legitimate TLS-terminating trusted proxies).

This PR adds a self-contained **pre-handshake** `verifyClient` gate on the gateway `WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, so unauthenticated or forged clients never complete the HTTP 101 upgrade. This is the WebSocket-upgrade sibling of the HTTP ingress CSRF work already on `main` (#102834, #96486) and complements the origin-allowlist work in #98924 (which decides *which* origins pass, not *when/how the gate runs*). The existing post-handshake origin check in `connect-admission.ts` is unchanged and remains authoritative for role-scoped decisions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pre-handshake beats post-handshake** — a rejected client never gets a live socket.
- **Reuses the shared `checkBrowserOrigin`** rather than reinventing origin logic.
- **All strictness is opt-in and default-off** (`gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation`, `rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders`, `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests`), so existing deployments have **zero behavior change**. Non-browser clients (CLI, native apps) send no `Origin` and pass through; they authenticate post-handshake as today.
- **Trusted proxies are correctly exempted** from the proto-mismatch check — a TLS-terminating proxy legitimately presents plaintext to the gateway.

## User Impact

- Network-exposed gateways gain a pre-handshake defense against forged forwarded headers and cross-site WebSocket CSRF, with **no config change required** for existing users (all new behavior opt-in).
- Operators who want stricter posture can enable:
  - `gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation` — reject duplicate / comma-chained sensitive proxy headers and proto contradictions.
  - `gateway.security.rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders` — reject proxy headers from non-trusted peers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` — reject `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` / `cross-origin` WebSocket upgrades. **Off by default**; opt in only when every legitimate browser WS client is same-origin to the gateway.

## Evidence

### Current-head live WebSocket Upgrade proof

A real `node:http` server with a real `ws.WebSocketServer({ noServer: true, verifyClient })`, wired through the **production** `createGatewayVerifyClient` from this branch, was sent real HTTP Upgrade requests over a raw socket (the same wire path the production gateway uses — not a mock). Sensitive-header duplicate/chain cases are sent as raw duplicate header lines, because Node's normalized `req.headers` collapses them before handler code runs; `validateSensitiveHeaders` reads `req.rawHeaders` to catch exactly that.

```
== LIVE WS UPGRADE PROOF (head 5924fb1314e) ==

[duplicate x-forwarded-for (two raw lines)] (strict ON)
    [verify-client] verifyClient: strict header validation failed: x-forwarded-for
    HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request  -> REJECTED ✓

[duplicate Host (raw; Node drops 2nd in req.headers)] (strict ON)
    [verify-client] verifyClient: strict header validation failed: host
    HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request  -> REJECTED ✓

[comma-chained x-forwarded-for] (strict ON)
    [verify-client] verifyClient: strict header validation failed: x-forwarded-for
    HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request  -> REJECTED ✓

[native client, no Origin] (default)
    HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  -> ACCEPTED ✓

[trusted proxy + proxy headers] (strict ON + trusted)
    HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  -> ACCEPTED ✓

[duplicate xff but strict OFF (default)] (no breakage)
    HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  -> ACCEPTED ✓

RESULT: ALL CASES PASSED
```

This directly proves the two reviewer asks on the current head:
- **Duplicate sensitive-header rejection** — cases 1–3 show `strictHeaderValidation` rejects duplicate and comma-chained `x-forwarded-for` / `host` at the 101 boundary, reading from `req.rawHeaders` so Node's normalized view can't hide the duplicates.
- **Accepted compatibility case** — case 4 (native client, no Origin) and case 5 (trusted proxy presenting proxy headers under `strictHeaderValidation`) both complete the upgrade; case 6 confirms the default-off posture introduces zero breakage for the existing duplicate-header traffic some proxies emit.

### Full behavior matrix (unit + wire, this branch)

| # | Scenario | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Native client, no Origin | `101 Switching Protocols` |
| 2 | Loopback-alias browser (`localhost`→`127.0.0.1`, cross-site) — v2026.4.15 contract | `101 Switching Protocols` |
| 3 | Allowed browser Origin (allowlist) | `101 Switching Protocols` |
| 4 | Disallowed browser Origin | `403 Forbidden` |
| 5 | Cross-site WS rejection (flag opt-in) | `403 Forbidden` |
| 6 | Forwarded-header contradiction (IPv6) | `400 Bad Request` |
| 7 | Forwarded-header agreement (IPv6 bracketed+port vs bracketed) | `101 Switching Protocols` |
| 8 | Proto mismatch from untrusted peer | `400 Bad Request` |
| 9 | Proto mismatch from trusted proxy (TLS-terminating) | `101 Switching Protocols` |
| 10 | Untrusted proxy headers (opt-in) | `403 Forbidden` |
| 11 | Literal `null` Origin (opaque context) | `403 Forbidden` |

Tests: `src/gateway/server/verify-client.test.ts` (11/11 passing), `tsgo` core typecheck clean, `oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean on touched files.

## Scope

- **In scope:** `src/gateway/server/verify-client.ts` (new, wired at `server-runtime-state.ts`), `src/gateway/forwarded-headers.ts` (validators), their tests, and the `gateway.security.*` config surface in `src/config/types.gateway.ts` + `src/config/zod-schema.gateway.ts`.
- **Out of scope:** the `#98924` allowlist-wildcard contract and the broader `gateway.browserOrigins` policy direction.

## Related

- Sibling enforcement: #98924 (`allowedOriginPatterns`).
- Prior art this complements (addressed on `main`): #102834 (HTTP ingress CSRF under `auth.mode=none`), #96486 (CSRF via `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`, reused verbatim here).
